pages.title: Rivers that meet their banks
pages.subtitle: Continuous exposed bars and better shallow-water geometry

blocks.text: River bars now blend continuously along connected cross-sections. At the tested problem reach, a 4.8-metre bed jump across ten centimetres of travel fell to about three centimetres. Inner bends retain broader exposed sediment; outer banks stay narrower and more vegetated.

images.caption: Revised bars on the same reach. The selected anchor and camera differ; this is not an aligned pixel comparison.
The revised exposed bar from ground level. Existing generated ground textures are retained.

blocks.text: This improves the banks, not the entire river network. Some courses remain too ribbon-like, and a separate legacy bank-overlap defect remains unresolved.

pages.title: Finite ponds, continuous shores
pages.subtitle: Small water bodies stay inside their actual basins

blocks.text: Coarse ground triangles could bridge a pond hollow while water disappeared beneath them, or extend wet ground beyond its finite shore. Encountered ponds now receive bounded basin refinement, and the water follows the same curved datum as the terrain.

images.caption: Actual in-game shoreline review. This near view is unchanged by the later reduction in distant-only refinement.

blocks.text: Refinement applies to finite ponds that need it, rather than tessellating the whole ocean. Distant ponds use a smaller constraint pattern. Terrain, water, vegetation and saved-history checks accompany the visual review.
Wetland vegetation remains a separate art and placement task. Correct water coverage alone does not make a convincing reed bed or swamp.

pages.title: Crescent dune fields
pages.subtitle: A distinct sand landscape alongside the existing connected ridges

blocks.text: Separated crescent dunes add curved crests, tapered horns and a steeper lee face. Their placement uses existing sandy terrain, seasonal wind diversity and a bounded terrain-suitability proxy. It is not a full airflow or sand-transport simulation.

images.caption: An actual generated crescent field, viewed obliquely. Medium vegetation settings.
Ground-level view of the dune face. No extra scenery objects or new rendering passes were added.

blocks.text: The star-dune experiment was rejected after in-game inspection and is disabled. These captures show the retained crescent implementation.

pages.title: Performance and limits
pages.subtitle: Moving tests, explicit conditions, and unfinished work

blocks.text: RTX 4060 / Ryzen 7 5700X, 1920 ? 1080, Medium, 6 km view, 45-second moving loops with rapid turns. All recorded frames focused. These are selected routes, not proof of the worst location in the world.

Mean performance is comparable on these routes. The maxima are individual observations, not a proven spike improvement. Final results use the clean full build; an earlier package with worse timing was rejected.

The absolute 100 FPS floor is still unmet. Frame spikes remain. A legacy river-bank overlap defect, overly regular smaller rivers and broad wetland vegetation are follow-ups. Rejected star-dune captures are excluded from this report.
